text.p: Thunderstorms and lightning twice forced a suspension of play midway during the second round of the Loch Lomond World Invitational on Thursday.
Play was first suspended with thunder and lightning in the area at 1515 local (1415GMT) and heavy rain prevented a resumption for 2-3/4 hours.
But the players had barely returned to the course when more lightning triggered the siren and forced the them to head for shelter again without playing any further shots.
It was not clear if play would recommence on Thursday though several hours of daylight remained.
One player, Welshman Paul Affleck, was disqualified after continuing to play after the first klaxon sounded to cease play immediately.
Just under half the 153-man field had completed their rounds and three groups had still to begin.
British Open champion Tom Lehman headed the scoreboard on 10 under par when he was forced off the course after 11 holes of his round.

He was one shot ahead of joint first-round leader Joakim Haeggman of Sweden, who had moved to nine under through 14 holes after sharing the first round lead with Paul Curry of England on 63, eight under par.
Steve Jones, the 1996 U.S. Open champion, was the leader in the clubhouse on eight under par after a second round of 65. Curry was also eight under with two holes to complete.
Tournament director Mike Stewart said the event could still be completed on Saturday as scheduled if there was good weather the next two days.
He said there was no option to complete the event on Sunday because so many players were involved in final qualifying on Sunday and Monday for next week's British Open at Royal Troon.
